pinouts.alias_policy: common-package-intersection: GPIO labels common to every reviewed package for the family or matching family_part; no physical package is assigned to an alias

limitations: All verified SYSCTRL peripheral-reset controls assert low (write 0) and release high (write 1). Upstream Rcc field references cannot encode polarity; consumers must read this sidecar rather than use active-high STM32 reset assumptions.
APBEN1/APBEN2 are register banks for one PCLK, not evidence for PCLK1/PCLK2.
Scoped peripheral-local muxes cannot be represented faithfully by upstream unscoped Rcc::Mux Field. Such records are partial and must not be emitted with a fabricated fixed PCLK.
Kernel fixed-clock facts denote input source before peripheral prescalers, baud dividers, timer count-mode routing, or optional digital filters; they are not guaranteed counter/output frequencies.
CW32 documents Sleep and DeepSleep; upstream Stop1/Stop2/Standby enum is not directly vendor-backed. Apply an explicitly documented conservative software policy if emitting Rcc.
Shared gates/reset lines require shared ownership or reference counting. Resetting one member can affect all members.

Clock metadata: 22 complete identities, 30 independently verified controls; 11 partial identities remain in the factual sidecar. RccControl carries actual reset polarity, write keys and shared groups without inferring a kernel. Stop1 is only a conservative build policy, not a CW32 hardware mode.

limitations: SVD-imported registers are not silicon-tested or a guarantee the vendor SVD is error-free.
Generic family features have no memory-size assertion; exact part features source memory separately.

Exact-part core pins and physical package pins come only from reviewed package tables; package-less aliases use an explicitly documented common-package GPIO intersection when configured. Input-only/output capability remains in pinout sidecars.

Only configured reviewed clock and DMA projections are imported. Verified reset polarity, write keys and shared controls are transported independently in rcc_control; unresolved kernel identities are withheld.
Digital alternate-function routes are imported only for explicitly reviewed profiles and filtered by package pins. Analog/special routes and flash geometry remain incomplete.
Read-clear, write-one-clear and reset-value semantics are not represented by chiptool IR.
SVD correctly exposes two DMA channels. Vendor header erroneously defines channels3-5. CW32F020 User Manual CN V1.4 section8.2 p122 and section8.7 p134 confirm only two.

F020 CRC has eight CRC16 modes only (0-7), unlike copied SDK/SVD CRC32 declarations. The CRC32-named result register is retained solely as a 32-bit bus view with a corrected 16-bit valid field; see docs/f020-serial-compatibility.md. CR.MODE retains its documented 4-bit layout; values8-15 remain unsupported. DR8/DR16/DR32 input widths are all documented.

All verified SYSCTRL peripheral-reset controls assert low (write 0) and release high (write 1). Upstream Rcc field references cannot encode polarity; consumers must read this sidecar rather than use active-high STM32 reset assumptions.
APBEN1/APBEN2 are register banks for one PCLK, not evidence for PCLK1/PCLK2.
Scoped peripheral-local muxes cannot be represented faithfully by upstream unscoped Rcc::Mux Field. Such records are partial and must not be emitted with a fabricated fixed PCLK.
Kernel fixed-clock facts denote input source before peripheral prescalers, baud dividers, timer count-mode routing, or optional digital filters; they are not guaranteed counter/output frequencies.
CW32 documents Sleep and DeepSleep; upstream Stop1/Stop2/Standby enum is not directly vendor-backed. Apply an explicitly documented conservative software policy if emitting Rcc.
Shared gates/reset lines require shared ownership or reference counting. Resetting one member can affect all members.
